SHOCKING Secret! — Use This Before Bed And GROW Your Hair BACK! 😱🌙 | Dr. Jason Fung


Could the secret to healthier, fuller-looking hair begin with what you do before going to bed? Hair thinning, excessive shedding, and a widening hairline can affect confidence, self-esteem, and how we feel about ourselves, especially after age 50. But understanding the science behind hair growth may help you make smarter decisions about your nighttime hair-care routine. In this educational video, we explore the connection between scalp health, hair follicles, nutrition, hormones, and healthy nighttime habits—and why consistency matters when supporting stronger, healthier hair.


TIMESTAMPS:
00:00 – 😱 The Surprising Connection Between Bedtime and Hair Health  
01:20 – 🧬 Understanding Why Hair Starts Thinning  
02:45 – 🌙 The Nighttime Hair-Care Secret Explained  
04:10 – 🌿 Supporting Healthy Scalp Conditions  
05:35 – 🥗 Essential Nutrients for Healthy Hair  
07:00 – 💪 Protein, Iron, and Zinc: What Your Hair Needs  
08:30 – 🩸 Hormones and Their Role in Hair Loss  
10:00 – 😴 Sleep, Stress, and Hair Health  
11:30 – 🚫 Common Hair-Care Mistakes to Avoid  
13:00 – 👨‍⚕️ When Hair Loss Needs Medical Attention  
14:30 – ❤️ Building Healthier Habits After 50  
15:30 – 🌟 Final Thoughts: Protect Your Hair Health


KEYWORDS:
hair regrowth, hair growth after 50, natural hair care, hair loss treatment, nighttime hair routine, thinning hair solutions, healthy scalp, stronger hair naturally, hair follicle health, prevent hair thinning, hair growth tips, aging and hair loss, hair nutrition, healthy hair habits, hair shedding, scalp care routine, hair health for seniors, female hair loss, male pattern baldness, Dr Jason Fung.


HASHTAGS:
#HairGrowth #HairRegrowth #HairLoss #HealthyHair #HairCare #ThinningHair #NaturalHairCare #ScalpHealth #HairGrowthTips #HairAfter50 #HairHealth #HealthyAging #HairFollicles #NighttimeRoutine #HairNutrition #SeniorHealth #HealthyLifestyle #DrJasonFung


DISCLAIMER:
This video is for educational and informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. It is not a substitute for professional diagnosis or treatment. Hair loss can have several underlying causes, including hormonal changes, nutritional deficiencies, genetics, and medical conditions. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional or dermatologist before starting new treatments or supplements. Individual results may vary.


REFERENCES:
- Stenn KS, Paus R. Controls of hair follicle cycling. *Physiological Reviews*. 2001;81(1):449–494.
- Almohanna HM et al. The Role of Vitamins and Minerals in Hair Loss: A Review. *Dermatology and Therapy*. 2019;9:51–70.
- Guo EL, Katta R. Diet and Hair Loss: Effects of Nutrient Deficiency and Supplement Use. *Dermatology Practical & Conceptual*. 2017;7(1):1–10.
- Phillips TG, Slomiany WP, Allison R. Hair Loss: Common Causes and Treatment. *American Family Physician*. 2017;96(6):371–378.

Hair loss or alopecia is a problem that
I often get asked about. What can we do
for hair loss? How can we grow new hair?
This is Jason Fung, a famous health
expert known worldwide. She strongly
supports holistic and natural health
with many testimonials backing her
methods. In this video, Jason will
reveal the causes of hair loss, offer
tips on how to prevent it, share natural
remedies, and provide advice on
achieving longer, healthier hair. So
stay tuned. Well, first of all, we have
to put the detective hat on and find out
why there is hair loss. So what would be
some of the most common causes of hair
loss? Well, one friend of mine, she
always dyed her hair. She was showing
gray hair from a very early age, and so
from about the age of 30, she began to
dye her hair. Now you can get a hair dye
made of henna, and henna is a plant that
can dye your hair and that is not toxic.
But my friend did not use that one. She
used a chemical hair dye, and little by
little it was killing off her hair
follicles where the hair grows. So it
can be chemicals on the hair. Another
friend of mine did not like her very
curly hair, and so all her life
from probably about her late teens right
up until her 50s, she straightened her
hair. Now the solutions that they use to
straighten the hair or for people with
straight hair that want curly hair is a
very toxic chemical. So what happens is
if a person wants to straighten their
hair, what the hairdresser does is pull
the hair over great big rods like that.
And so the curly hair, it is this curly
of course, gets pulled over them and
that straightens it. But if a person has
got straight hair and they want curly
hair, well the rods are that big and
they stretch the hair around and around
and around. So whether it is to
straighten the hair or whether it is to
curl the hair, they put this toxic
solution on. It is a strong chemical,
and what it does is it breaks all the
little joins in because hair has all
these little joins like this. So what it
does is it breaks the joins, breaks the
joins, and then it is molded of course
around either there for the curl or
there for the straight. And then when
all of those little bonds are broken and
it has been stretched into a certain
shape, they rinse off that chemical and
then they put another chemical on to set
it, so to set the bonds together, and
then that sets the hair structure as
straight or as curly. So basically that
is how the hair is permed. Proper
nutrition is vital for healthy hair, and
deficiencies in iron, zinc, biotin, or
protein can lead to hair loss.
Maintaining a diet rich in vitamins and
minerals is essential. Certain
medications for conditions like high
blood pressure, cancer, or depression
may also contribute to hair loss, so
consult your doctor if you suspect this.
Understanding these factors is key to
adopting effective treatments and
lifestyle changes for healthier hair. I
have also seen in some areas where
people braid their hair really, really
tightly, you will often see that they
have got hair loss around here where
you've got that weight. You have got
that constant weight on the hair which
can really just keep pulling the hair
out and then the follicles are damaged.
So no matter how it happens, we must
stop what is causing the damage. That is
first. If you do not turn the tap off,
you are still mopping up in the other
corner. Sometimes I see hair loss in a
hormonal imbalance. So if it is a
hormonal imbalance, then the hormones
must be balanced back again. Hair loss
is often driven by hormonal changes.
Fluctuations in hormones like
testosterone can result in androgenetic
alopecia, which causes hair thinning in
both men and women. Disruptions in
hormone levels during pregnancy,
menopause, or due to thyroid disorders
can also lead to increased hair
shedding. Additionally, elevated
cortisol levels from stress can cause
temporary hair loss, which is called
telogen effluvium. Sometimes high
stress, if someone goes through a very
stressful situation, one of the
reactions can be hair loss. So what can
you do to bring it back again? Ah, there
is one more that I did not mention, and
that is anemia. If a person is anemic,
it can cause hair loss. So what is
anemic? Anemic means very low iron in
the blood, and anemia can be caused
because of heavy blood loss at period
time. A lot of women suffer from that,
and that can cause anemia, and the
anemia can cause the hair loss. So to
resolve that again, watch my lecture on
hormones, boost the progesterone, get
the estrogen down, then there will not
be the heavy blood loss every month, and
the person will not be anemic anymore.
And so again, the hair can grow. Another
cause of anemia can be low hydrochloric
acid because iron is bound up in food,
and it needs acid to liberate it from
food. So it is very important that the
person ensure they have nice strong
hydrochloric acid. Simple way to ensure
that is to have a quarter of a teaspoon
of cayenne pepper and a little bit of
water before every meal. If you are
finding that a little bit hard, you can
have the juice of a lemon before every
meal. Important to leave a break between
meals. Important not to drink water with
your meals because that dilutes the
hydrochloric acid. Also important to
have a very happy, relaxed environment
at the meal table. I target those points
in more detail on my lecture on the gut.
So the causes of hair loss can be
anemia, it can be high stress, it can be
a hormonal imbalance, and it can be
damage. That is just physical damage.
This has been done to the hair
follicles. Iron deficiency reduces
hemoglobin production, reducing oxygen
flow to cells including hair follicles.
Since follicles need oxygen and
nutrients to grow, a lack of it weakens
hair, making it thinner and prone to
shedding. But what can you do to the
scalp to encourage the hair to grow
again? You can make a mix that you can
put on your hair, and this mix is Let us
make up the mix. So half a cup of
coconut oil and half a cup of castor
oil. Castor oil is a very thick oil, but
castor oil penetrates deeper than any
other oil. So when that is put onto the
scalp, it penetrates even deeper.
Coconut oil is a very nourishing oil. It
is an antifungal oil, antibacterial oil.
But what you also can put with that So
now you have got a cup of oil there. To
that cup of oil, you can add 10 drops of
rosemary essential oil. Rosemary is a
herb that is specific for the scalp,
rosemary essential oil. So you could
make up this mix in a jar and mix it
very very well, and maybe once a week
you massage it into the scalp. Your hair
will be very oily, of course, but you
massage it into the scalp. Just even the
massaging into the scalp stimulates
blood supply to the hair follicles. That
castor oil penetrates very deep, and
wherever it penetrates, it can revive
life into that area. And the coconut
also is a very nourishing oil, and the
rosemary essential oil stimulates. Every
herb stimulates different parts of the
body, and this rosemary herb is specific
for the scalp. The massaging So leave it
in as much as you can. Maybe you choose
a Sunday when you are going to be home
all day, and at the end of the day you
wash out. Now you might need to put
shampoo on a couple of times to get all
that oil out. Just use a little bit of
hot water and then a nice amount of
shampoo. Also good to know is that
hibiscus flowers help strengthen hair by
providing essential vitamins, minerals,
and amino acids that nourish the scalp
and support healthy growth. To use,
crush three to four flowers with coconut
oil into a paste, apply it to your scalp
and hair and leave it for 30 minutes
before rinsing.
For best results, repeat this treatment
once or twice a week. And if it is still
a little bit greasy, maybe shampoo it
again. Now that brings us to the
shampoo. There is something that you
must keep right away from,
and it is called sodium lauryl sulfate.
Sodium lauryl sulfate is what is in many
shampoos, and sodium lauryl sulfate
kills the hair follicles. it is
important to take a magnifying glass
into the shop and read the labels.
places like Whole Foods, Sprouts, Trader
Joe's, where they have a lot of health
foods, so they have a lot of supplements
and they have a more healthier brand of
products. So have a look for a shampoo
that has no So we have got to make sure
you realize no sodium lauryl sulfate.
Because the sodium lauryl sulfate is a
chemical that causes the foaming of the
shampoo, and that sodium lauryl sulfate
has the ability to kill the hair
follicles in the scalp. So please keep
away from that. You can get some very
nice coconut-based shampoos. When
selecting a shampoo, choose sulfate-free
formulas to help minimize hair loss and
support scalp health. Seek out products
containing biotin, keratin, vitamins,
and essential oils. Ingredients like
aloe vera, rosemary, and tea tree can
further improve hair quality. Opt for
shampoos that are both gentle and
effective for the best care of your hair
and scalp. Exercise. What exercise does
is it increases the circulation of the
blood to the extremities, and the scalp
is considered an extremity. So exercise
daily, especially the high intensity
interval training, the high intensity
interval training because of the periods
of very high intensity that really gets
the blood moving out to the extremities.
So that should be done daily. And
hydration, keep well hydrated. Remember
the rule of thumb is eight glasses to
100 lb body weight. That is a good rule
of thumb, too, to know how much to how
much water to give the children.
Nourishment. We need to nourish that
scalp from the inside because your scalp
is fed by your blood. That is why when
you exercise you get more blood to the
area. But when you get the blood to the
area, you want it be well watered.
Exercise will automatically put the
oxygen in there. And nourishment. We
need to be having a high fiber diet,
high fiber. We also need to be having
generous amounts of protein. Here is
your legumes, your nuts, your seeds, so
generous proteins. Proteins are the
building blocks of the body and healthy
fats. So there is your nuts, your seeds,
your avocados, coconut coconut and olive
oil. Eating a diverse range of fruits
and vegetables is essential for overall
health including scalp health.
B vitamins, especially biotin, are
crucial for hair health and can be found
in foods like eggs, leafy greens and
whole grains. Omega-3 fatty acids
present in fish such as salmon as well
as flax seeds and walnuts also support a
healthy scalp.
Sleep. You want to heal, you got to get
8 hours.
8 hours not negotiable every night. The
sleep is vital. The sleep is not
negotiable. If you are not used to that
much sleep, little by little by little
you can train yourself back into
sleeping longer. Rome was not built in a
day, but little by little by little as
you take those steps that are conducive
to good sleep. Breakfast like a king,
lunch like a queen, light or no evening
meal, going to bed early, soft lights,
soft music, fresh air coming in, nice
clean natural fiber sheets and pillows.
All of this is conducive to a good
night's sleep. Getting enough sleep is
essential for preventing hair loss as it
reduces stress and promotes hair
follicle repair. Quality sleep regulates
hormones like cortisol and melatonin
crucial for hair growth and improves
blood circulation to nourish follicles.
A consistent sleep schedule is key for
healthy hair. So we might as well start
with hair. The color of the hair a lot
has to do with genetics. My husband is
white and both his parents were white at
50 and my mother died at 51 with brown
hair and my father just passed at 92
with graying hair but a a of black now.
There is my brother, then me and three
younger sisters, and none of us have
gray hair because from both sides of our
family there was not gray. Now my
father's sister, she died at 68 with
brown hair, and at the funeral I saw my
three cousins, her sons, that I have not
seen for a long time, and they are all
gray. So they have probably got that a
little bit from the father's side. So
Michael and I are interesting because we
are both extremes really. Both his
parents white at 50, and my parents are
not gray. But I also know that people
have claimed to get the color back in
their hair by drinking a lot of green
drinks. Now what green drinks contain is
a lot of minerals.
And when you consider what we talked
about this afternoon, that the mineral
content of the soil is about 50% less
what it was 50 years ago, that a lot of
the foods today have less minerals in
them. You see in Australia the soil is
just the plants are just put in year
after year after year. What should
happen is when a crop comes out of the
ground, then the soil should be fed with
rich compost because every time a crop
is in the ground it is taking new
nutrients out, and if you do not replace
the nutrients, then the next crop that
is grown there is going to be nutrient
deficient. So that makes sense, does it
not? So really looking at agriculture is
the only way to change the farming
habits. And unfortunately, because there
is big dollars made in big industry and
growing lots of stuff in super
phosphate, I do not know how that will
ever turn around. But you can do the
best you can. You can grow as much as
you can. You can buy the best quality
that you can, and you can have green
drinks. So how do you have green drinks?
Well, you can buy chlorophyll, you can
buy green barley powder, you can buy
wheatgrass powder, you can buy super
greens. So basically taking that three
times a day, making sure you have lots
of greens in your daily salad will will
it. You do not lose the minerals when
you cook your greens. You only lose your
minerals if you throw the water away
that you cook them in. What about
dandruff? Dandruff can often happen when
using shampoo with sodium lauryl
sulfate. It can also happen when a
person is on a high sugar diet because
that basically feeds the dandruff. So
getting a better shampoo and doing a
coconut oil rub or soak every month
ideally and also looking at your diet
because we are what we eat. And I have a
book at home called Pure, White and
Deadly and the whole book is about
sugar. And Dr. Yudkin, the author, he
maintains that it should be banned. It
is so dangerous and we do not need to
eat sugar because we have got honey and
maple syrup. And you have got a sugar
here on your islands which is an
excellent sugar. It is palm sugar or
coconut sugar. It is just the
crystallized nectar from the palm
flower. So that is hair. Green drinks
are good for you because they have a lot
of chlorophyll. This helps fight off
free radicals and supports detoxing.
Chlorophyll can also lower inflammation,
help wounds heal, and increase red blood
cell production. Plus, green drinks are
full of important vitamins and minerals
like A, C, K, and B vitamins, which are
great for your health, immune system,
and keeping your skin and hair healthy.
Although green drinks will not stop your
hair from turning gray, eating a diet
rich in nutrients can help your hair by
supporting melanin production and
overall health. And that is it again for
today, guys. I hope you found these
insights helpful for promoting healthier
hair and overall well-being.
